questions.q:
Match the compounds given in column I with the corresponding most stable Carbocations formed by each, as given in Column II, when they undergo acidic dehydration in presence of Conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$.
No.Column INo.Column II
A2-Methylbutan-1-olP$(CH_3)_2\overset{+}{C} - CH(CH_3)_2$
BButan-2-olQ$CH_3 - CH_2 - CH_2 - \overset{+}{C}H_2$
C3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-olR$(CH_3)_2\overset{+}{C} - CH_2 - CH_3$
DButan-1-olS$CH_3 - \overset{+}{C}H - CH_2 - CH_3$
questions.solution:
For 2-Methylbutan-1-ol (A): The initial carbocation is $CH_3CH_2CH(CH_3)CH_2^{+}$. A 1,2-hydride shift occurs to form the more stable tertiary carbocation $(CH_3)_2C^{+}CH_2CH_3$, which corresponds to R.

For Butan-2-ol (B): The initial carbocation is $CH_3CH^{+}CH_2CH_3$, which is a secondary carbocation. This is already stable and corresponds to S.

For 3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-ol (C): The initial carbocation is $CH_3CH^{+}C(CH_3)_3$. A 1,2-methyl shift occurs to form the more stable tertiary carbocation $(CH_3)_2C^{+}CH(CH_3)_2$, which corresponds to P.

For Butan-1-ol (D): The initial carbocation is $CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2^{+}$. Although primary, it is the only remaining option Q, which represents the primary carbocation $CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_2^{+}$.

Matching the results: A=R, B=S, C=P, D=Q.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{R} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{P} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{Q}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound $[\mathrm{A}]\left(\mathrm{C}_5 \mathrm{H}_{12} \mathrm{O}\right)$, on reaction with conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ at $443 \mathrm{~K}$ gives $[\mathrm{B}]$ as one of the products. Compound [B] undergoes further reaction with $\mathrm{O}_3$ and $\mathrm{Zn} / \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ to give Propanone and Ethanal as products. Identify compound [A]
questions.solution:
The molecular formula of compound [A] is $C_5H_{12}O$, which corresponds to a saturated alcohol or ether. Since it reacts with conc. $H_2SO_4$ at $443 K$ to form an alkene [B], [A] is an alcohol.

The reaction of [B] with $O_3$ followed by $Zn/H_2O$ (reductive ozonolysis) yields propanone ($CH_3COCH_3$) and ethanal ($CH_3CHO$).

The structure of the alkene [B] can be reconstructed by joining the carbonyl carbons of the products with a double bond. Propanone is $CH_3-C(=O)-CH_3$ and ethanal is $CH_3-CH=O$. Removing the oxygen atoms and joining the carbons gives $CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_3$. This is 2-methylbut-2-ene.

Compound [A] is an alcohol that undergoes dehydration to form 2-methylbut-2-ene. Among the given options, 3-methylbutan-2-ol ($CH_3-CH(OH)-CH(CH_3)_2$) can undergo dehydration via a carbocation rearrangement or direct elimination to form 2-methylbut-2-ene as the major product according to Zaitsev's rule.

Specifically, 3-methylbutan-2-ol dehydrates to form 2-methylbut-2-ene as the most stable alkene product.

Answer: 3-Methylbutan-2-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect regarding acetal and ketal formation when Propanal and Propanone are separately reacted with Ethanol in presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ gas.
options: Rate of formation of acetal is greater than that of ketal formation.
Both Propanal and Propanone undergo Nucleophilic addition reaction during this process.
Propanal and Ethanol should be taken in the approximate ratio of $1: 2$ for acetal formation.
Anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ gas decreases the electrophilicity of the Carbonyl Carbon.
questions.solution:
Propanal is an aldehyde and Propanone is a ketone. Aldehydes are more reactive towards nucleophilic addition than ketones due to both steric and electronic factors. Thus, the rate of acetal formation from propanal is greater than the rate of ketal formation from propanone.

Both reactions involve the nucleophilic attack of ethanol on the carbonyl carbon, which is a nucleophilic addition reaction.

Acetal formation is a reversible reaction. To shift the equilibrium towards the product (acetal), an excess of alcohol is typically used, or water is removed. The stoichiometric ratio for the reaction $RCHO + 2R'OH \rightarrow RCH(OR')_2 + H_2O$ is $1:2$.

Anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ acts as an acid catalyst. It protonates the carbonyl oxygen, which increases the positive charge density on the carbonyl carbon, thereby increasing its electrophilicity and making it more susceptible to nucleophilic attack by ethanol. Therefore, the statement that $\mathrm{HCl}$ decreases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon is incorrect.

Answer: Anhydrous $\mathrm{HCl}$ gas decreases the electrophilicity of the Carbonyl Carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the Reagents I and II to be used in the course of the given reactions.
options: $\text { Reagent I: } \mathrm{Zn} / \mathrm{Hg} \text { in conc. } \mathrm{HCl} \quad \text { Reagent II: }\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_2\right]^{+}$
$\text { Reagent I: DIBAL- } \mathrm{H} / \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \quad \text { Reagent II: conc. } \mathrm{KOH} / \text { heat }$
questions.solution:
Starting material [A] is 1-chloro-1-formylcyclohexan-4-one.

$Cu^{2+}/OH^-$ oxidises the aldehyde to carboxylic acid (ketone unaffected). [B] = 1-chlorocyclohexan-4-one-1-carboxylic acid.

$C_2H_5OH/H^+$ esterifies the carboxylic acid. [C] = ethyl 1-chlorocyclohexan-4-one-1-carboxylate.

Reagent I (DIBAL-H/$H_2O$): Reduces the ester group selectively to an aldehyde, giving 1-chloro-4-oxocyclohexane-1-carbaldehyde. This compound has an aldehyde on a quaternary carbon (no $\alpha$-hydrogens).

Reagent II (conc. KOH/heat): An aldehyde without $\alpha$-hydrogens undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction (self-oxidation and reduction) with concentrated base.

Reagent I: DIBAL-H/$H_2O$, Reagent II: conc. KOH/heat.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A Carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ when reacted with Methyl magnesium bromide followed by hydrolysis gave product $\mathrm{Y}$. When $\mathrm{Y}$ is heated with $\mathrm{Cu}$ at $573 \mathrm{~K}$, it gave $\mathrm{Z}$ (2- Methylbut-2-ene) as one of the products. Identify $\mathrm{X}$.
questions.solution:
The reaction of a carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ with $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by hydrolysis yields an alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$.

Heating alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ with $\mathrm{Cu}$ at $573 \mathrm{~K}$ is a dehydrogenation reaction for primary and secondary alcohols, or a dehydration reaction for tertiary alcohols. Since the product $\mathrm{Z}$ is 2-methylbut-2-ene, which is an alkene, the reaction is a dehydration of a tertiary alcohol.

The structure of 2-methylbut-2-ene is $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.

The tertiary alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ that dehydrates to form 2-methylbut-2-ene is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, which has the structure $\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$.

The alcohol $\mathrm{Y}$ (2-methylbutan-2-ol) is formed by the reaction of a ketone with methylmagnesium bromide. Specifically, the reaction of butan-2-one ($\mathrm{CH}_{3}-\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{3}$) with $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$ followed by hydrolysis yields 2-methylbutan-2-ol.

Therefore, the carbonyl compound $\mathrm{X}$ is butan-2-one.

Answer: Butanone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the final product formed when Toluene undergoes the following series of reactions?
questions.solution:
Toluene reacts with conc. $HNO_{3}$ and $H_{2}SO_{4}$ (nitrating mixture) to undergo electrophilic aromatic substitution. Since the methyl group is ortho/para directing, the major product [B] is p-nitrotoluene.

Reduction of p-nitrotoluene with $Fe/HCl$ converts the nitro group ($-NO_{2}$) into an amino group ($-NH_{2}$), yielding [C], which is p-toluidine (4-methylaniline).

Reaction of p-toluidine with acetic anhydride $(CH_{3}CO)_{2}O$ results in the acetylation of the amino group to form [D], which is 4-methylacetanilide.

Answer: 4-methylacetanilide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which one of the following shows the correct increasing order of basic nature of the given compounds?
A: Phenylmethanamine
B: N-Ethylethanamine
C:N, N-Dimethylaniline
D : N, N-Dimethylmethanamine
questions.solution:
The basicity of amines depends on the availability of the lone pair on the nitrogen atom. Electron-donating groups increase basicity, while electron-withdrawing groups or resonance delocalization decrease it.

Compound A is Phenylmethanamine ($C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}NH_{2}$), a primary amine where the lone pair is not delocalized into the ring, but the phenyl group exerts a weak inductive effect. It is more basic than aromatic amines but less basic than aliphatic amines.

Compound B is N-Ethylethanamine ($(C_{2}H_{5})_{2}NH$), a secondary aliphatic amine. Secondary aliphatic amines are generally the most basic due to the strong inductive effect of two alkyl groups and favorable solvation.

Compound C is N,N-Dimethylaniline ($C_{6}H_{5}N(CH_{3})_{2}$), a tertiary aromatic amine. The lone pair on the nitrogen is delocalized into the benzene ring, making it the least basic among the given compounds.

Compound D is N,N-Dimethylmethanamine ($(CH_{3})_{3}N$), a tertiary aliphatic amine. While it has three electron-donating methyl groups, its basicity is often lower than secondary amines due to steric hindrance and solvation effects in aqueous media.

Comparing the basicity: C (aromatic) < A (primary aliphatic/aromatic-like) < D (tertiary aliphatic) < B (secondary aliphatic).

Thus, the increasing order is C < A < D < B.

Answer: C < A < D < B

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Aniline undergoes reactions with reagents given in the order shown
(i) Aqueous $\mathrm{Br}_2$
(ii) $\mathrm{NaNO}_2 / \mathrm{HCl} / 0^0 \mathrm{C}$
(iii) Hypophosphorous acid
What is the product formed at the end of these reactions?
questions.solution:
Aniline reacts with aqueous $\text{Br}_2$ to form $2,4,6$-tribromoaniline as the major product due to the strong activating effect of the $-\text{NH}_2$ group.

The $2,4,6$-tribromoaniline then reacts with $\text{NaNO}_2 / \text{HCl}$ at $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ to undergo diazotization, forming the corresponding diazonium salt, $2,4,6$-tribromobenzenediazonium chloride.

Finally, the reaction of the diazonium salt with hypophosphorous acid ($\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$) and water results in the reduction of the diazonium group to a hydrogen atom, yielding $1,3,5$-tribromobenzene as the final product.

Answer: $1,3,5$ - Tribromobenzene

questions.q:
Match the Hormones listed in Column I with their characteristics listed in Column II
No.HormoneNo.Characteristics
AAdrenal CortexPMediates responses to external stimuli.
BEpinephrineQSteroid hormone.

questions.solution:
Adrenal cortex produces steroid hormones like cortisol and aldosterone. Malfunction or hyposecretion of the adrenal cortex leads to Addison's disease. Thus, A matches with S.

Epinephrine is a catecholamine hormone secreted by the adrenal medulla that mediates rapid responses to external stimuli, often referred to as the fight-or-flight response. Thus, B matches with P.

Estrogen is a primary female sex hormone and is classified as a steroid hormone. Thus, C matches with Q.

Thyroxine is an iodinated derivative of the amino acid tyrosine, produced by the thyroid gland. Thus, D matches with R.

Combining these, we get A=S, B=P, C=Q, D=R.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{P} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{Q} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{R}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the 2 chemical tests which is not answered by Glucose having an open chain structure
[A] Reaction with Schiff's reagent and with Sodium bisulphite
[B] Reaction with $\mathrm{HCN}$ and with $\mathrm{HI}$
[C] Reaction with $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ and with Acetic anhydride
[D] Reaction with aqueous Bromine and with Hydroxylamine
questions.solution:
Glucose predominantly exists in a cyclic hemiacetal form, so the free aldehyde concentration is extremely low.

Due to this, glucose fails two characteristic aldehyde tests:

It does not restore the pink colour of Schiff's reagent, and it does not form an addition compound with sodium bisulphite ($NaHSO_3$).

All other reactions (with $HCN$, $HI$, $HNO_3$, acetic anhydride, aqueous bromine, hydroxylamine) do occur successfully.

The two tests not answered by glucose correspond to option [A].

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are 4 statements about Insulin. Which of these statement/(s) is/are correct?
[A] Insulin is a globular protein consisting of 51 Amino acids.
[B] Insulin is constituted of 3 polypeptide chains linked together.
[C] Insulin is constituted of 2 polypeptide chains linked together by disulphide bonds.
[D] The 3 polypeptide chains in Insulin are linked together by Hydrogen bonding.
questions.solution:
Insulin is a peptide hormone produced by the beta cells of the pancreatic islets. It is a globular protein composed of 51 amino acids. Therefore, statement [A] is correct.

Insulin consists of two polypeptide chains, known as the A-chain and the B-chain. The A-chain contains 21 amino acids, and the B-chain contains 30 amino acids. These two chains are linked together by two inter-chain disulphide bonds, and there is also an intra-chain disulphide bond within the A-chain. Therefore, statement [C] is correct, while statement [B] and statement [D] are incorrect.

Answer: [A] & [C]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A sweet smelling organic compound $[\mathrm{A}]\left(\mathrm{C}_9 \mathrm{H}_{10} \mathrm{O}_2\right)$ undergoes acid hydrolysis to form an acid [B].
Compound [B] further reacts with Ammonia followed by heating to yield [C].
Compound $[\mathrm{C}]$ when reacted with $\mathrm{Br}_2$ in caustic potash gave compound $[\mathrm{D}]\left(\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H} 7 \mathrm{~N}\right)$ which gives a white precipitate with aqueous $\mathrm{Br}_2$.
Identify compounds $[\mathrm{A}]$ & $[\mathrm{D}]$
questions.solution:
Compound [A] has the molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_9\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O}_2$. Acid hydrolysis of [A] yields an acid [B]. Since [A] is a sweet-smelling ester, it is likely an ester of benzoic acid. Ethyl benzoate ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOCH}_2\mathrm{CH}_3$) has the formula $\mathrm{C}_9\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O}_2$.

Hydrolysis of ethyl benzoate gives benzoic acid [B] ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{COOH}$) and ethanol. Benzoic acid reacts with ammonia to form ammonium benzoate, which upon heating yields benzamide [C] ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{CONH}_2$).

Compound [C] (benzamide) reacts with $\mathrm{Br}_2$ in caustic potash ($\mathrm{KOH}$), which is the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction. This converts the amide group $-\mathrm{CONH}_2$ into an amine group $-\mathrm{NH}_2$, yielding aniline [D] ($\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{NH}_2$).

Aniline has the molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_7\mathrm{N}$ and reacts with aqueous $\mathrm{Br}_2$ to form 2,4,6-tribromoaniline, which is a white precipitate. Thus, [A] is ethyl benzoate and [D] is aniline.

Answer: A: Ethyl benzoate D: Aniline

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the pair of molecules, both of which have positive values of Dipole moment.
questions.solution:
The dipole moment of a molecule depends on its geometry and the polarity of its bonds. A molecule has a non-zero dipole moment if its bond dipoles do not cancel each other out.

$\mathrm{BF}_3$ has a trigonal planar geometry. The three $\mathrm{B-F}$ bond dipoles are equal and oriented at $120^{\circ}$ to each other, resulting in a net dipole moment of zero.

$\mathrm{CCl}_4$ has a tetrahedral geometry. The four $\mathrm{C-Cl}$ bond dipoles are equal and arranged symmetrically, resulting in a net dipole moment of zero.

$\mathrm{NF}_3$ has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with a lone pair on the nitrogen atom. The bond dipoles of the three $\mathrm{N-F}$ bonds and the lone pair do not cancel out, resulting in a net dipole moment of approximately $0.24 \text{ D}$.

$\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ has a tetrahedral geometry, but because the atoms attached to the central carbon are not identical (three $\mathrm{Cl}$ atoms and one $\mathrm{H}$ atom), the bond dipoles do not cancel, resulting in a net dipole moment of approximately $1.01 \text{ D}$.

Comparing the options, both $\mathrm{NF}_3$ and $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ have non-zero (positive) dipole moments.

Answer: $\mathrm{NF}_3$ & $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
On the basis of VSEPR theory, match the molecules listed in Column I with their shapes given in Column II.
No.Column INo.Column II
A$ClF_3$PSee-saw
B$BrF_5$QPentagonal bipyramidal
C$SF_4$RSquare pyramidal
D$IF_7$ST-shaped
questions.solution:
For $\mathrm{ClF_3}$, the central atom $\mathrm{Cl}$ has $7$ valence electrons. It forms $3$ bonds with $\mathrm{F}$ atoms and has $2$ lone pairs. The steric number is $3 + 2 = 5$, which corresponds to trigonal bipyramidal geometry. With $2$ lone pairs in equatorial positions, the shape is T-shaped. Thus, $\mathrm{A} = \mathrm{S}$.

For $\mathrm{BrF_5}$, the central atom $\mathrm{Br}$ has $7$ valence electrons. It forms $5$ bonds with $\mathrm{F}$ atoms and has $1$ lone pair. The steric number is $5 + 1 = 6$, which corresponds to octahedral geometry. With $1$ lone pair, the shape is square pyramidal. Thus, $\mathrm{B} = \mathrm{R}$.

For $\mathrm{SF_4}$, the central atom $\mathrm{S}$ has $6$ valence electrons. It forms $4$ bonds with $\mathrm{F}$ atoms and has $1$ lone pair. The steric number is $4 + 1 = 5$, which corresponds to trigonal bipyramidal geometry. With $1$ lone pair in an equatorial position, the shape is see-saw. Thus, $\mathrm{C} = \mathrm{P}$.

For $\mathrm{IF_7}$, the central atom $\mathrm{I}$ has $7$ valence electrons. It forms $7$ bonds with $\mathrm{F}$ atoms and has $0$ lone pairs. The steric number is $7$, which corresponds to pentagonal bipyramidal geometry. Thus, $\mathrm{D} = \mathrm{Q}$.

Comparing these results, we have $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{S}$, $\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{R}$, $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{P}$, and $\mathrm{D}=\mathrm{Q}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{R} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{P} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{Q}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are 4 molecular species/ions. Identify the species/ion which exhibits diamagnetic nature.
$[\mathrm{A}]=\mathrm{N}_2^{+} \quad[\mathrm{B}]=\mathrm{O}_2^{-} \quad[\mathrm{C}]=\mathrm{B}_2 \quad[\mathrm{D}]=\mathrm{C}_2$
questions.solution:
The molecular orbital configuration for each species is determined based on the number of electrons.

For $\mathrm{N_2^{+}}$ (13 electrons):
$\sigma_{1s}^{2}\,\sigma_{1s}^{*2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{*2}\,\pi_{2p_x}^{2}\,\pi_{2p_y}^{2}\,\sigma_{2p_z}^{1}$
Since there is one unpaired electron in the $\sigma_{2p_z}$ orbital, it is paramagnetic.

For $\mathrm{O_2^{-}}$ (17 electrons):
$\sigma_{1s}^{2}\,\sigma_{1s}^{*2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{*2}\,\sigma_{2p_z}^{2}\,\pi_{2p_x}^{2}\,\pi_{2p_y}^{2}\,\pi_{2p_x}^{*2}\,\pi_{2p_y}^{*1}$
Since there is one unpaired electron in the $\pi_{2p_y}^{*}$ orbital, it is paramagnetic.

For $\mathrm{B_2}$ (10 electrons):
$\sigma_{1s}^{2}\,\sigma_{1s}^{*2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{*2}\,\pi_{2p_x}^{1}\,\pi_{2p_y}^{1}$
According to Hund's rule, the two electrons in the degenerate $\pi$ orbitals remain unpaired, making it paramagnetic.

For $\mathrm{C_2}$ (12 electrons):
$\sigma_{1s}^{2}\,\sigma_{1s}^{*2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{2}\,\sigma_{2s}^{*2}\,\pi_{2p_x}^{2}\,\pi_{2p_y}^{2}$
All electrons are paired; therefore, $\mathrm{C_2}$ is diamagnetic.

Answer: [D]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
For the reaction $\mathrm{Cl}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}+2 \mathrm{NO}_{(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{NOCl}_{(\mathrm{g})}$, the following data was obtained:
Experiment No.Initial concentration of $Cl_2$ (M)Initial concentration of NO (M)Initial reaction rate (M/min)
I0.150.150.60
II0.300.151.20
III0.150.302.40
IV0.250.252.78
Identify the order of the reaction with respect to $\mathrm{Cl}_2, \mathrm{NO}$ and the value of Rate constant.
options: $\text { Order with respect to } \mathrm{Cl}_2=0 \quad \text { Order with respect to } \mathrm{NO}=1 \quad \mathrm{k}=8.0 \mathrm{~min}^{-1}$
$\text { Order with respect to } \mathrm{Cl}_2=1 \quad \text { Order with respect to } \mathrm{NO}=1 \quad \mathrm{k}=26.66 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \mathrm{Lmin}^{-1}$
$\text { Order with respect to } \mathrm{Cl}_2=2 \quad \text { Order with respect to } \mathrm{NO}=1 \quad \mathrm{k}=355.5 \mathrm{~mol}^{-2} \mathrm{~L}^2 \mathrm{~min}^{-1}$
$\text { Order with respect to } \mathrm{Cl}_2=1 \quad \text { Order with respect to } \mathrm{NO}=2 \quad \mathrm{k}=177.7 \mathrm{~mol}^{-2} \mathrm{~L}^2 \mathrm{~min}^{-1}$
questions.solution:
The rate law for the reaction is given by $Rate = k[Cl_2]^x [NO]^y$.

Using data from Experiment I and II:
$0.60 = k(0.15)^x (0.15)^y$
$1.20 = k(0.30)^x (0.15)^y$
Dividing the two equations: $\dfrac{1.20}{0.60} = \left(\dfrac{0.30}{0.15}\right)^x \Rightarrow 2 = 2^x \Rightarrow x = 1$.

Using data from Experiment I and III:
$0.60 = k(0.15)^1 (0.15)^y$
$2.40 = k(0.15)^1 (0.30)^y$
Dividing the two equations: $\dfrac{2.40}{0.60} = \left(\dfrac{0.30}{0.15}\right)^y \Rightarrow 4 = 2^y \Rightarrow y = 2$.

The rate law is $Rate = k[Cl_2]^1 [NO]^2$.

Calculating the rate constant $k$ using Experiment I:
$0.60 = k(0.15)(0.15)^2$
$0.60 = k(0.15)(0.0225)$
$0.60 = k(0.003375)$
$k = \dfrac{0.60}{0.003375} = 177.77 \text{ M}^{-2} \text{ min}^{-1}$.

Thus, the order with respect to $Cl_2$ is 1, the order with respect to $NO$ is 2, and $k \approx 177.7 \text{ mol}^{-2} \text{ L}^2 \text{ min}^{-1}$.

Answer: $\text { Order with respect to } \mathrm{Cl}_2=1 \quad \text { Order with respect to } \mathrm{NO}=2 \quad \mathrm{k}=177.7 \mathrm{~mol}^{-2} \mathrm{~L}^2 \mathrm{~min}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A given chemical reaction is represented by the following stoichiometric equation.

$3 X+2 Y+\dfrac{5}{2} Z \rightarrow P_1+P_2+P_3$ The rate of reaction can be expressed as _________.
questions.solution:
For a general reaction $aA + bB + cC \rightarrow Products$, the rate of reaction is given by:

Rate $= -\dfrac{1}{a} \dfrac{d[A]}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{b} \dfrac{d[B]}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{c} \dfrac{d[C]}{dt}$

Given the reaction $3X + 2Y + \dfrac{5}{2}Z \rightarrow P_1 + P_2 + P_3$, the rate of reaction is:

Rate $= -\dfrac{1}{3} \dfrac{d[X]}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{d[Y]}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{5/2} \dfrac{d[Z]}{dt} = -\dfrac{2}{5} \dfrac{d[Z]}{dt}$

Equating the terms:

$-\dfrac{1}{3} \dfrac{d[X]}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{d[Y]}{dt} \Rightarrow \dfrac{2}{3} \dfrac{d[X]}{dt} = \dfrac{d[Y]}{dt}$

$-\dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{d[Y]}{dt} = -\dfrac{2}{5} \dfrac{d[Z]}{dt} \Rightarrow \dfrac{d[Y]}{dt} = \dfrac{4}{5} \dfrac{d[Z]}{dt}$

Combining these, we get:

$\dfrac{2}{3} \dfrac{d[X]}{dt} = \dfrac{d[Y]}{dt} = \dfrac{4}{5} \dfrac{d[Z]}{dt}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}\left(\dfrac{d[X]}{d t}\right)=\left(\dfrac{d[Y]}{d t}\right)=\dfrac{4}{5}\left(\dfrac{d[Z]}{d t}\right)$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The rate constant for the reaction $\mathrm{A} \rightarrow \mathrm{B}+\mathrm{C}$ at $500 \mathrm{~K}$ is given as $0.004 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. At what temperature will the rate constant become $0.014 \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ ? $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}}$ for the reaction is $18.231 \mathrm{~kJ}$.
questions.solution:
The Arrhenius equation is given by $\ln \left( \dfrac{k_2}{k_1} \right) = \dfrac{E_a}{R} \left( \dfrac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2} \right)$.

Given values are $k_1 = 0.004 \text{ s}^{-1}$, $T_1 = 500 \text{ K}$, $k_2 = 0.014 \text{ s}^{-1}$, and $E_a = 18.231 \text{ kJ/mol} = 18231 \text{ J/mol}$. The gas constant $R = 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Substituting the values into the equation:

$\ln \left( \dfrac{0.014}{0.004} \right) = \dfrac{18231}{8.314} \left( \dfrac{T_2 - 500}{500 T_2} \right)$

$\ln(3.5) = 2192.8 \times \left( \dfrac{T_2 - 500}{500 T_2} \right)$

$1.25276 = 4.3856 \left( \dfrac{T_2 - 500}{T_2} \right)$

$0.28565 = 1 - \dfrac{500}{T_2}$

$\dfrac{500}{T_2} = 1 - 0.28565 = 0.71435$

$T_2 = \dfrac{500}{0.71435} \approx 700 \text{ K}$.

Answer: 700 K

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The time required for $80 \%$ of a first order reaction is "$y$" times the half-life period of the same reaction. What is the value of "$y$"?
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by $k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \left( \dfrac{[A]_0}{[A]_t} \right)$.

The half-life period $t_{1/2}$ is given by $t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k}$.

For $80\%$ completion, $[A]_t = [A]_0 - 0.80[A]_0 = 0.20[A]_0$.

The time $t_{80\%}$ is $t_{80\%} = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \dfrac{[A]_0}{0.20[A]_0} \right) = \dfrac{2.303}{k} \log(5)$.

Using $\log(5) \approx 0.699$, $t_{80\%} = \dfrac{2.303 \times 0.699}{k} = \dfrac{1.61}{k}$.

We are given $t_{80\%} = y \times t_{1/2}$, so $y = \dfrac{t_{80\%}}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{1.61/k}{0.693/k} = \dfrac{1.61}{0.693} \approx 2.32$.

Answer: 2.32

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Given below are 4 graphs [A], [B], [C] and [D] Identify the 2 graphs that represent a Zero order reaction?
questions.solution:
For a zero order reaction, the rate law is given by $\text{Rate} = k[R]^0 = k$. This implies that the rate of the reaction is independent of the concentration of the reactant $[R]$. Thus, a plot of $\text{Rate}$ versus $[R]$ is a horizontal straight line, which corresponds to graph [D].

The integrated rate equation for a zero order reaction is $[R] = -kt + [R]_0$. This is in the form of a linear equation $y = mx + c$, where $y = [R]$, $x = t$, $m = -k$, and $c = [R]_0$. Therefore, a plot of $[R]$ versus time is a straight line with a negative slope equal to $-k$, which corresponds to graph [C].

Graph [A] represents a first order reaction where $\ln[R]$ versus time is a straight line with slope $-k$. Graph [B] represents a first order reaction where $[R]$ versus time is an exponential decay curve. Therefore, graphs [C] and [D] represent a zero order reaction.

Answer: [C] and [D]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A d - block metal $\mathrm{X}(\mathrm{Z}=26)$ forms a compound $[\mathrm{X}(\mathrm{CN})_2(\mathrm{CO})_4]^{+}$. Calculate its spin magnetic moment value.
questions.solution:
The metal X is Iron (Fe) with atomic number $Z = 26$. The electronic configuration of Fe is $[Ar] 3d^{6} 4s^{2}$.

In the complex $[Fe(CN)_{2}(CO)_{4}]^{+}$, let the oxidation state of Fe be $x$. Since $CN^{-}$ is $-1$ and $CO$ is neutral, we have $x + 2(-1) + 4(0) = +1$, which gives $x = +3$.

The electronic configuration of $Fe^{3+}$ is $[Ar] 3d^{5}$.

Both $CN^{-}$ and $CO$ are strong field ligands. According to crystal field theory, strong field ligands cause pairing of electrons in the $d$-orbitals. For a $d^{5}$ configuration with strong field ligands, the electrons pair up in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals: $(t_{2g})^{5} (e_{g})^{0}$.

The number of unpaired electrons $n = 1$.

The spin magnetic moment $\mu$ is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM. Substituting $n = 1$, we get $\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73$ BM.

Answer: 1.73 BM

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A Coordination compound is represented by the formula $[\mathrm{CoBr}_3(e n) x]$. This compound required one mole of $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ to form a pale yellow precipitate of $\mathrm{AgBr}$. What is the value of $\mathrm{x}$ in the compound?
questions.solution:
The coordination compound is given as $[CoBr_3(en)x]$. The reaction with $AgNO_3$ produces a pale yellow precipitate of $AgBr$, which indicates that one bromide ion is present outside the coordination sphere as a counter ion.

The reaction can be represented as $[CoBr_2(en)x]Br + AgNO_3 \rightarrow [CoBr_2(en)x]NO_3 + AgBr(s)$.

The coordination number of Cobalt(III) in such complexes is typically 6. The ethylenediamine (en) ligand is bidentate, occupying 2 coordination sites. Let the number of bromide ions inside the coordination sphere be $y$. Then the total coordination number is $2(en) + y(Br) = 6$.

Since there are 3 bromide ions in total and 1 is outside, $y = 2$. Thus, $2(en) + 2(Br) = 6$, which implies $2(2) + 2 = 6$. This is consistent with the coordination number of 6.

The formula is $[CoBr_2(en)x]Br$. Comparing this with the given formula $[CoBr_3(en)x]$, we see that $x$ represents the number of ethylenediamine ligands. Since $2(en)$ is required to satisfy the coordination number, $x = 2$.

Answer: 2

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement from the following.
options: A tetrahedral complex of the type $[\mathrm{Ma}_2 \mathrm{b}_2]$ does not show geometrical isomerism
In a coordination entity of the type $[\mathrm{Ma} 2(\mathrm{bb})_2]^{2+}$ only the cis-isomer is optically active
Coordination entities of the type $[\mathrm{Ma}_3 \mathrm{b}_3]$ do not exhibit geometrical isomerism
Square planar complex Â of the type [Mabcd] has 3 possible geometrical isomers
questions.solution:
In a tetrahedral complex of the type $[Ma_2b_2]$, all positions are equivalent relative to each other, meaning there is no distinction between cis and trans positions. Thus, it does not show geometrical isomerism. This statement is correct.

For a coordination entity of the type $[Ma_2(bb)_2]^{2+}$, where $(bb)$ is a symmetrical bidentate ligand, the cis-isomer lacks a plane of symmetry and is optically active, while the trans-isomer possesses a plane of symmetry and is optically inactive. This statement is correct.

Coordination entities of the type $[Ma_3b_3]$ exhibit facial (fac) and meridional (mer) geometrical isomers. Therefore, the statement that they do not exhibit geometrical isomerism is incorrect.

A square planar complex of the type $[Mabcd]$ has three possible geometrical isomers, which are obtained by fixing one ligand and arranging the others in different positions relative to it. This statement is correct.

Answer: Coordination entities of the type $[\mathrm{Ma}_3 \mathrm{b}_3]$ do not exhibit geometrical isomerism

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the incorrect statement from the following
options: $\mathrm{Cu}$ (I) compounds in aqueous medium undergo disproportionation reaction
$\mathrm{MoO}_3$ and $\mathrm{WO}_3$ are not as strong oxidants as $\mathrm{CrO}_3$
The ability of Fluorine to stabilise the higher oxidation states of transition metals exceeds that of Oxygen
$\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ is a stronger reducing agent than $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$
questions.solution:
(1) Correct: $Cu^+$ is unstable in aqueous medium due to the much higher hydration energy of $Cu^{2+}$. It undergoes disproportionation: $2Cu^+(aq) \to Cu^{2+}(aq) + Cu(s)$.

(2) Correct: Oxidising power decreases down Group 6. $CrO_3$ is a strong oxidant while $MoO_3$ and $WO_3$ are much weaker.

(3) Incorrect: Oxygen can stabilise higher oxidation states through multiple bonding (e.g., in oxoanions like $MnO_4^-$, $CrO_4^{2-}$). The ability of oxygen to stabilise higher oxidation states is superior to that of fluorine in many cases. So the statement that fluorine exceeds oxygen is incorrect.

(4) Correct: $Cr^{2+}(d^4)$ is oxidised to $Cr^{3+}(d^3$, stable $t_{2g}^3)$. $E°(Cr^{3+}/Cr^{2+}) = -0.41$ V, while $E°(Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}) = +0.77$ V. Lower reduction potential means $Cr^{2+}$ is a stronger reducing agent than $Fe^{2+}$.

The incorrect statement is (3).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following ions in the increasing order of their $\Delta H_{(\text {hydration})}$ values.
$\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}, \mathrm{Co}^{2+}, \mathrm{Mn}^{2+}, \mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$
questions.solution:
The enthalpy of hydration ($\Delta H_{\text{hydration}}$) for transition metal ions is primarily determined by the charge-to-size ratio, which is inversely proportional to the ionic radius. As the atomic number increases across the 3d series for ions of the same charge ($+2$), the effective nuclear charge increases, leading to a decrease in ionic radius.

The ionic radii for the given $M^{2+}$ ions follow the order: $\text{Mn}^{2+} \gt \text{Cr}^{2+} \gt \text{Co}^{2+} \gt \text{Ni}^{2+}$.

Since $\Delta H_{\text{hydration}}$ is directly proportional to the charge density (which is inversely proportional to the radius), a smaller ionic radius results in a more negative (larger magnitude) enthalpy of hydration. Therefore, the magnitude of hydration energy increases as the ionic radius decreases.

The order of increasing magnitude of $\Delta H_{\text{hydration}}$ is $\text{Mn}^{2+} \lt \text{Cr}^{2+} \lt \text{Co}^{2+} \lt \text{Ni}^{2+}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}\lt \mathrm{Cr}^{2+}\lt \mathrm{Co}^{2+}\lt \mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Match the compounds given in Column I with their characteristic features listed in Column II
No.Column INo.Column II
A$La(OH)_3$PAcidic in nature
B$Mn_2O_7$QLeast basic
C$Lu(OH)_3$RInterstitial compound
D$Fe_3H$SMost basic
questions.solution:
The basicity of lanthanoid hydroxides $\mathrm{Ln}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ decreases as the ionic radius of the lanthanoid ion $\mathrm{Ln}^{3+}$ decreases due to lanthanoid contraction. $\mathrm{La}^{3+}$ has the largest ionic radius, making $\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ the most basic, while $\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ has the smallest ionic radius, making $\mathrm{Lu}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ the least basic. Thus, $\mathrm{A} = \mathrm{S}$ and $\mathrm{C} = \mathrm{Q}$.

$\mathrm{Mn}_2\mathrm{O}_7$ is an oxide of manganese in a high oxidation state ($+7$), which makes it acidic in nature. Thus, $\mathrm{B} = \mathrm{P}$.

$\mathrm{Fe}_3\mathrm{H}$ is a non-stoichiometric hydride of iron, which is classified as an interstitial hydride (or metallic hydride). Thus, $\mathrm{D} = \mathrm{R}$.

Combining these, we get $\mathrm{A} = \mathrm{S}$, $\mathrm{B} = \mathrm{P}$, $\mathrm{C} = \mathrm{Q}$, and $\mathrm{D} = \mathrm{R}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{S} \quad \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{P} \quad \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{Q} \quad \mathrm{D}=\mathrm{R}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The permanganate ion in acid medium acts as an oxidant and gets converted to its lower oxidation state. What would be the spin only magnetic moment of such reduced manganese ion?
questions.solution:
In an acidic medium, the permanganate ion ($MnO_{4}^{-}$) acts as an oxidizing agent and is reduced to the manganese(II) ion ($Mn^{2+}$).

The oxidation state of manganese in $MnO_{4}^{-}$ is $+7$. In the acidic medium, the half-reaction is $MnO_{4}^{-} + 8H^{+} + 5e^{-} \rightarrow Mn^{2+} + 4H_{2}O$.

The electronic configuration of the manganese atom ($Z=25$) is $[Ar] 3d^{5} 4s^{2}$.

The electronic configuration of the $Mn^{2+}$ ion is $[Ar] 3d^{5}$.

In the $3d^{5}$ configuration, there are $5$ unpaired electrons ($n=5$).

The spin-only magnetic moment ($\mu$) is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ BM, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

Substituting $n=5$: $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{5 \times 7} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ BM.

Answer: 5.92 BM

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The cell reaction is $\mathrm{Cd}(s) + 2\mathrm{H}^{+}(aq) \rightarrow \mathrm{Cd}^{2+}(aq) + \mathrm{H}_{2}(g)$.

The standard cell potential $E^{0}_{cell}$ is calculated as $E^{0}_{cathode} - E^{0}_{anode}$.

Given $E^{0}(\mathrm{H}^{+}/\mathrm{H}_{2}) = 0.00 \text{ V}$ and $E^{0}(\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cd}) = -0.40 \text{ V}$.

$E^{0}_{cell} = 0.00 - (-0.40) = 0.40 \text{ V}$.

Using the Nernst equation at $298 \text{ K}$:

$E_{cell} = E^{0}_{cell} - \dfrac{0.0591}{n} \log \dfrac{[\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}] P_{\mathrm{H}_{2}}}{[\mathrm{H}^{+}]^{2}}$

Here $n = 2$, $[\mathrm{Cd}^{2+}] = 0.01 \text{ M}$, $[\mathrm{H}^{+}] = 0.02 \text{ M}$, and $P_{\mathrm{H}_{2}} = 0.8 \text{ atm}$.

$E_{cell} = 0.40 - \dfrac{0.0591}{2} \log \dfrac{0.01 \times 0.8}{(0.02)^{2}}$

$E_{cell} = 0.40 - 0.02955 \log \dfrac{0.008}{0.0004}$

$E_{cell} = 0.40 - 0.02955 \log(20)$

Since $\log(20) = \log(2 \times 10) = 0.3010 + 1 = 1.3010$.

$E_{cell} = 0.40 - 0.02955 \times 1.3010$

$E_{cell} = 0.40 - 0.03844 = 0.36156 \text{ V} \approx 0.3616 \text{ V}$.

Answer: 0.3616 V

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $0.1 \mathrm{M}$ solution of $\mathrm{AgNO}_3$ is taken in a Conductivity cell and a potential difference of $40 \mathrm{~V}$ is applied across the ends of a column of this solution whose diameter is $4.0 \mathrm{~cm}$ and length of the column is $12 \mathrm{~cm}$. The current used is $0.4 \mathrm{~A}$. The Molar conductivity of the solution is _________.
questions.solution:
The resistance $R$ of the solution is given by Ohm's law: $R = \dfrac{V}{I} = \dfrac{40 \text{ V}}{0.4 \text{ A}} = 100 \Omega$.

The area of cross-section $A$ of the column is $\pi r^2$. Given diameter $d = 4.0 \text{ cm}$, the radius $r = 2.0 \text{ cm}$. Thus, $A = \pi \times (2.0 \text{ cm})^2 = 4\pi \text{ cm}^2 \approx 12.566 \text{ cm}^2$.

The cell constant $G^{*}$ is given by $\dfrac{l}{A}$, where $l = 12 \text{ cm}$. So, $G^{*} = \dfrac{12}{4\pi} = \dfrac{3}{\pi} \text{ cm}^{-1} \approx 0.9549 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

The conductivity $\kappa$ is given by $\kappa = \dfrac{G^{*}}{R} = \dfrac{3/\pi}{100} = \dfrac{3}{100\pi} \text{ S cm}^{-1} \approx 0.009549 \text{ S cm}^{-1}$.

The molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ is calculated using the formula $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{1000 \times \kappa}{C}$, where $C = 0.1 \text{ M}$.

Substituting the values: $\Lambda_m = \dfrac{1000 \times (3 / (100\pi))}{0.1} = \dfrac{30}{\pi \times 0.1} = \dfrac{300}{\pi} \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Calculating the value: $\Lambda_m \approx \dfrac{300}{3.14159} \approx 95.493 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Rounding to the nearest option, we get $95.5 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Answer: $95.5 \mathrm{~Scm}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are 4 equations showing Molar conductivities at infinite dilution of various electrolytes. Which one of them represents the correct equation?
$\begin{aligned}
& \left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{N a B r}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{N a C l}=\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{KCl}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{KBr}} \\
& \left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{HCl}}+\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{KOH}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{KCl}}=\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}} \\
& \left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{KBr}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{NaBr}}=\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{NaBr}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{Nal}} \\
& \left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{N H_4 \mathrm{Cl}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{NO}_3}=\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{N H_4 \mathrm{Cl}}-\left(\Lambda_m^0\right)_{N H 4 B r}
\end{aligned}$
questions.solution:
Using Kohlrausch's law, expanding Equation 2 LHS: $(A^0_m)_{HCl} + (A^0_m)_{KOH} - (A^0_m)_{KCl}$

$= [\lambda^0(H^+) + \lambda^0(Cl^-)] + [\lambda^0(K^+) + \lambda^0(OH^-)] - [\lambda^0(K^+) + \lambda^0(Cl^-)]$

$= \lambda^0(H^+) + \lambda^0(OH^-)$

$= (A^0_m)_{H_2O}$ = RHS

Equation 2 is correct. The cancellation of $\lambda^0(Cl^-)$ and $\lambda^0(K^+)$ on both sides confirms LHS = RHS.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Propane in presence of $\mathrm{O}_2$ gas undergoes complete combustion to produce $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$. The required $\mathrm{O}_2$ for this combustion reaction was produced by the electrolysis of water. For what duration of time had water been electrolysed by passing $200 \mathrm{~A}$ current so that Oxygen gas produced could completely burn $44 \mathrm{~g}$ of Propane?
questions.solution:
The balanced chemical equation for the combustion of propane is:
$\text{C}_{3}\text{H}_{8} + 5\text{O}_{2} \rightarrow 3\text{CO}_{2} + 4\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$

The molar mass of propane ($\text{C}_{3}\text{H}_{8}$) is $3 \times 12 + 8 \times 1 = 44 \text{ g/mol}$.

Moles of propane = $\dfrac{44 \text{ g}}{44 \text{ g/mol}} = 1 \text{ mol}$.

From the stoichiometry, $1 \text{ mol}$ of propane requires $5 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_{2}$.

The electrolysis of water is given by:
$2\text{H}_{2}\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{H}_{2} + \text{O}_{2}$

For $1 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_{2}$ produced, $4 \text{ moles}$ of electrons are required (since each oxygen atom changes oxidation state from $-2$ to $0$, and there are $2$ oxygen atoms per $\text{O}_{2}$ molecule).

Total moles of electrons required for $5 \text{ mol}$ of $\text{O}_{2}$ = $5 \times 4 = 20 \text{ mol}$.

Using Faraday's law of electrolysis, $Q = n \times F = I \times t$, where $F \approx 96500 \text{ C/mol}$.

$20 \times 96500 = 200 \times t$

$t = \dfrac{20 \times 96500}{200} = 9650 \text{ seconds}$.

Converting to hours: $t = \dfrac{9650}{3600} \approx 2.68 \text{ hours}$.

Answer: 2.68 hours

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: From the following compounds, identify the one which is most acidic.
questions.solution:
The acidity of a compound is determined by the stability of its conjugate base. The more stable the conjugate base, the more acidic the compound.

Compound [A] is phenol, which forms a phenoxide ion. The negative charge on the oxygen is delocalized into the benzene ring.

Compound [B] is dicyclohexylmethanol, an aliphatic alcohol. It lacks resonance stabilization for its conjugate base and is the least acidic.

Compound [C] is p-nitrophenol. The nitro group ($-NO_2$) is a strong electron-withdrawing group (EWG) due to both its inductive effect ($-I$) and resonance effect ($-M$). This group significantly stabilizes the phenoxide ion by dispersing the negative charge, making p-nitrophenol more acidic than phenol.

Compound [D] is cyclohexanol, an aliphatic alcohol, which is less acidic than phenol.

Comparing the compounds, the presence of the strong electron-withdrawing $-NO_2$ group in [C] makes it the most acidic among the given options.

Answer: C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A statement of Assertion followed by a statement of Reason is given. Choose the correct answer out of the following options.
Assertion: The Eclipsed and the Staggered conformations of Ethane continuously flip from one form to the other. 
Reason: The torsional barrier between the Conformers of Ethane has a high value of about $50 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$ and this restricts free rotation around $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}$ bond.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct statement.
Both Assertion and Reason are incorrect statements.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect statement.
questions.solution:
The eclipsed and staggered conformations of ethane are conformers that interconvert rapidly at room temperature due to the low energy barrier for rotation around the carbon-carbon single bond. Thus, the assertion that they continuously flip is correct.

The torsional barrier for rotation in ethane is approximately $12.5 \text{ kJ/mol}$ (or $3 \text{ kcal/mol}$), not $50 \text{ kJ/mol}$. This energy barrier is low enough to allow for rapid rotation at room temperature, meaning rotation is not restricted. Therefore, the reason provided is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect statement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The stability of free radicals is primarily determined by resonance stabilization and hyperconjugation. The species are:

A: $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_3\dot{\mathrm{C}}$ (tert-butyl radical) - stabilized by 9 hyperconjugative hydrogens.

B: $(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5)_3\dot{\mathrm{C}}$ (triphenylmethyl radical) - stabilized by extensive resonance with three phenyl rings.

C: $(\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_5)_2\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}$ (diphenylmethyl radical) - stabilized by resonance with two phenyl rings.

D: $(\mathrm{CH}_3)_2\dot{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{H}$ (isopropyl radical) - stabilized by 6 hyperconjugative hydrogens.

Comparing the stabilization effects, resonance provides significantly greater stability than hyperconjugation. Therefore, the radicals with phenyl rings (B and C) are more stable than the alkyl radicals (A and D).

Among the resonance-stabilized radicals, B has three phenyl rings while C has two, making B more stable than C. Among the alkyl radicals, A has 9 hyperconjugative hydrogens while D has 6, making A more stable than D.

The decreasing order of stability is B > C > A > D.

Answer: B > C > A > D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product [D] formed when Reactant [A] $(M M 78 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{mol})$ undergoes the series of reactions shown
questions.solution:
The reactant [A] has a molar mass of $78$ g/mol, which corresponds to benzene ($C_6H_6$).

In the first step, benzene reacts with methyl chloride ($MeCl$) in the presence of a catalyst (Friedel-Crafts alkylation) to form toluene ($C_7H_8$).

In the second step, toluene reacts with $3$ moles of $Cl_2$ at $385$ K. This is a free-radical side-chain chlorination reaction, which replaces the three hydrogen atoms of the methyl group with chlorine atoms, yielding benzotrichloride ($C_6H_5CCl_3$) as product [C].

In the final step, benzotrichloride reacts with aqueous sodium hydroxide ($NaOH_{(aq)}$). The three chlorine atoms are replaced by hydroxyl groups to form a gem-triol intermediate ($C_6H_5C(OH)_3$), which is unstable and loses a water molecule to form benzoic acid ($C_6H_5COOH$) as product [D].

Answer: Benzoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following compounds in the decreasing order of reactivity towards $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{N}} 1$ reaction.
questions.solution:
The reactivity of alkyl halides towards the $S_{N}1$ reaction depends on the stability of the carbocation intermediate formed after the departure of the leaving group (chloride ion). The more stable the carbocation, the faster the $S_{N}1$ reaction.

Analyzing the structures:
[A] is 2-chloropentane, which forms a secondary ($2^{\circ}$) carbocation.
[B] is 1-chloropentane, which forms a primary ($1^{\circ}$) carbocation.
[C] is 2-chloro-2-methylbutane, which forms a tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) carbocation.
[D] is 1-chloro-2-methylpropane (isobutyl chloride), which forms a primary ($1^{\circ}$) carbocation, but it is sterically hindered compared to [B].

Comparing the stability of the carbocations:
Tertiary ($3^{\circ}$) > Secondary ($2^{\circ}$) > Primary ($1^{\circ}$).
Therefore, [C] is the most reactive ($3^{\circ}$), followed by [A] ($2^{\circ}$), then [B] ($1^{\circ}$), and finally [D] ($1^{\circ}$ with steric hindrance).

The order of reactivity is C > A > B > D.

Answer: C > A > B > D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following compounds when reacted with $\mathrm{NaOH}$ (aq) undergoes Substitution Nucleophilic Bimolecular reaction with retention of configuration?
questions.solution:
$S_N2$ reactions normally proceed with inversion of configuration (Walden inversion). Retention of configuration in $S_N2$ occurs via neighboring group participation (NGP), where a nearby group displaces the leaving group to form a cyclic intermediate, which is then opened by the nucleophile — resulting in a net double inversion (retention).

Option (1): $C_6H_{11}-CH(CH_3)-CH_2Cl$ is a primary alkyl chloride with a chiral centre at the $\beta$-carbon. The cyclohexyl ring with the adjacent chiral carbon allows NGP. The nucleophile attacks via double inversion, giving net retention of configuration.

Options (2), (3): Secondary alkyl halides — straightforward $S_N2$ gives inversion.

Option (4): Tertiary alkyl halide — $S_N2$ is sterically hindered; proceeds via $S_N1$ instead.

The compound that undergoes $S_N2$ with retention of configuration is option (1).

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\text { Identify }[\mathrm{B}] \text { and }[\mathrm{C}] \text { formed in the reactions given below. }$
questions.solution:
The starting material is $C_{3}H_{4}Br_{4}$. This is a tetrabromo derivative of propane. Reaction with Zn dust (dehalogenation) leads to the formation of an alkyne. Specifically, $CH_{3}-CBr_{2}-CHBr_{2}$ or $CH_{2}Br-CHBr-CH_{2}Br$ (though the formula $C_{3}H_{4}Br_{4}$ corresponds to $CH_{3}-CBr_{2}-CHBr_{2}$ or similar isomers) reacts with Zn dust to form propyne ($CH_{3}-C \equiv CH$) as product [B].

The reaction of propyne with $Hg^{2+}/H^{+}$ (Kucherov reaction) involves the hydration of the alkyne. The alkyne $CH_{3}-C \equiv CH$ undergoes hydration to form an enol intermediate, which tautomerizes to form propanone ($CH_{3}-CO-CH_{3}$) as product [C].

Propanone contains the $CH_{3}CO-$ group, which gives a positive iodoform test. Thus, [B] is propyne and [C] is propanone.

Answer: [B] Propyne [C] Propanone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following compounds shows Geometrical isomerism?
questions.solution:
Geometrical isomerism occurs in alkenes when each carbon atom of the double bond is attached to two different groups. We analyze the structure of each compound:

2-Methylhex-2-ene: $CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$. The carbon at position 2 is bonded to two identical methyl groups, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.

4-Methylhex-2-ene: $CH_3-CH=CH-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$. The carbon at position 2 is bonded to a hydrogen and a methyl group. The carbon at position 3 is bonded to a hydrogen and a sec-butyl group. Since both carbons of the double bond have different groups attached, this compound exhibits geometrical isomerism.

4-Methylhex-1-ene: $CH_2=CH-CH_2-CH(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_3$. The terminal carbon (position 1) is bonded to two identical hydrogen atoms, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.

2-Methylhex-1-ene: $CH_2=C(CH_3)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$. The terminal carbon (position 1) is bonded to two identical hydrogen atoms, so it does not show geometrical isomerism.

Answer: 4-Methylhex-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An unsaturated hydrocarbon $[\mathrm{A}]$ reacts with $\mathrm{HBr}$ in presence of Benzoyl peroxide to yield [B]
Compound [A] when reacted with cold, dilute alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ gave compound [C], 2-Methylbutane-2, 3-diol But when [A] is reacted with hot $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$, it yielded $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{COOH}$ and a compound [D] Identify compounds [A], [B] and [D]
questions.solution:
Compound [A] reacts with cold, dilute alkaline $\text{KMnO}_{4}$ to form 2-methylbutane-2,3-diol. This reaction is a syn-hydroxylation of an alkene. The structure of 2-methylbutane-2,3-diol is $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(OH)(CH}_{3})-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_{3}$. The corresponding alkene [A] is 2-methylbut-2-ene, which has the structure $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(CH}_{3})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_{3}$.

Reaction of 2-methylbut-2-ene with hot $\text{KMnO}_{4}$ (oxidative cleavage) breaks the double bond: $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(CH}_{3})=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_{3} \xrightarrow{\text{hot KMnO}_{4}} \text{CH}_{3}-\text{C(=O)}-\text{CH}_{3} + \text{CH}_{3}-\text{COOH}$. Here, $\text{CH}_{3}-\text{COOH}$ is acetic acid and [D] is propanone ($\text{CH}_{3}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_{3}$).

Reaction of 2-methylbut-2-ene with $\text{HBr}$ in the presence of benzoyl peroxide follows anti-Markovnikov addition. The radical mechanism leads to the formation of 2-bromo-3-methylbutane, as the bromine radical adds to the less substituted carbon of the double bond to form the more stable secondary radical intermediate.

Answer: [A] 2-Methylbut-2-ene [B] 2-Bromo-3-methylbutane [D] Propanone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
An aromatic hydrocarbon $[\mathrm{A}]\left(\mathrm{Molecular}\right.$ formula $\left.\mathrm{C}_9 \mathrm{H}_{12}\right)$, undergoes air oxidation followed by reaction with dil.
$\mathrm{HCl}$ to give [B] as one of the products
Compound [B] forms a white precipitate on treatment with $\mathrm{Br}_2(\mathrm{aq})$
Sodium salt of [B] reacts with $\mathrm{CO}_2$ at $400 \mathrm{~K}$ under high pressure followed by acid hydrolysis to give [C]
Compound [C] reacts with acetic anhydride / conc. $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ to form [D]
Identify compound $[\mathrm{D}]$
questions.solution:
The aromatic hydrocarbon [A] with molecular formula $C_9H_{12}$ that undergoes air oxidation (cumene process) is isopropylbenzene (cumene).

Air oxidation of cumene followed by treatment with dilute $HCl$ yields phenol and acetone as products. Compound [B] is phenol ($C_6H_5OH$), which forms a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol on treatment with $Br_2(aq)$.

The sodium salt of phenol (sodium phenoxide) reacts with $CO_2$ at $400 K$ under high pressure followed by acid hydrolysis (Kolbe-Schmitt reaction) to give salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) as compound [C].

Compound [C] (salicylic acid) reacts with acetic anhydride in the presence of conc. $H_2SO_4$ (acetylation) to form aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid), which is 2-acetoxybenzoic acid. This corresponds to the structure with a benzene ring having a $COOH$ group and an $OCOCH_3$ group at ortho positions.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of mono-chloro derivatives of Ethyl cyclohexane possible?
questions.solution:
Ethyl cyclohexane has the molecular formula $C_8H_{16}$. The structure consists of a cyclohexane ring with an ethyl group attached at one position.

The positions available for substitution are:
1. The alpha-carbon of the ethyl group (1 position).
2. The beta-carbon of the ethyl group (1 position).
3. The ring carbons: The carbon attached to the ethyl group (1 position), the ortho positions (2 equivalent positions), the meta positions (2 equivalent positions), and the para position (1 position).

Counting the distinct positions for chlorine substitution:
1. Alpha-carbon of ethyl group: 1 isomer.
2. Beta-carbon of ethyl group: 1 isomer.
3. Ring carbon attached to ethyl group: 1 isomer.
4. Ortho position on ring: 1 isomer.
5. Meta position on ring: 1 isomer.
6. Para position on ring: 1 isomer.

Total number of mono-chloro derivatives = 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 6.

Answer: 6

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $300 \mathrm{ml}$ of an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{NaOH}$ with $\mathrm{pH}$ value of 10 is mixed with $200 \mathrm{ml}$ of an aqueous solution of $\mathrm{HCl}$ with a $\mathrm{pH}$ value of 4. What will be the $\mathrm{pH}$ of the resultant solution at room temperature?
questions.solution:
For the NaOH solution, $\text{pH} = 10$, so $\text{pOH} = 14 - 10 = 4$.

$[\text{OH}^{-}] = 10^{-4} \text{ M}$.

Moles of $\text{OH}^{-} = 300 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L} \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol/L} = 3 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

For the HCl solution, $\text{pH} = 4$, so $[\text{H}^{+}] = 10^{-4} \text{ M}$.

Moles of $\text{H}^{+} = 200 \times 10^{-3} \text{ L} \times 10^{-4} \text{ mol/L} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

Since $\text{OH}^{-}$ reacts with $\text{H}^{+}$ to form water, the remaining moles of $\text{OH}^{-}$ are $3 \times 10^{-5} - 2 \times 10^{-5} = 1 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}$.

Total volume of the mixture $= 300 \text{ ml} + 200 \text{ ml} = 500 \text{ ml} = 0.5 \text{ L}$.

Resultant concentration of $\text{OH}^{-} = \dfrac{1 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol}}{0.5 \text{ L}} = 2 \times 10^{-5} \text{ M}$.

$\text{pOH} = -\log(2 \times 10^{-5}) = 5 - \log 2 = 5 - 0.301 = 4.699$.

$\text{pH} = 14 - 4.699 = 9.301$.

Answer: 9.301

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{~B}_4$ is a sparingly soluble salt with a solubility of $\mathrm{s} g / \mathrm{L}$. If the Molar mass of $\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{~B}_4$ is $\mathrm{Mg} / \mathrm{mol}$, what is the expression for its $\mathrm{K}_{\text {sp }}$ ?
questions.solution:
The salt $\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{B}_4$ dissociates in water as follows:

$\mathrm{A}_3 \mathrm{B}_4 (s) \rightleftharpoons 3 \mathrm{A}^{4+} (aq) + 4 \mathrm{B}^{3-} (aq)$

The solubility of the salt is given as $s$ g/L. The molar mass of the salt is $M$ g/mol. Therefore, the molar solubility $S$ in mol/L is given by:

$S = \dfrac{s}{M}$ mol/L

From the stoichiometry of the dissociation, the concentration of $\mathrm{A}^{4+}$ is $3S$ and the concentration of $\mathrm{B}^{3-}$ is $4S$.

The solubility product constant $K_{sp}$ is defined as:

$K_{sp} = [\mathrm{A}^{4+}]^3 [\mathrm{B}^{3-}]^4$

Substituting the concentrations in terms of $S$:

$K_{sp} = (3S)^3 (4S)^4$

$K_{sp} = (27 S^3) (256 S^4)$

$K_{sp} = 27 \times 256 \times S^7$

$K_{sp} = 6912 S^7$

Substituting $S = \dfrac{s}{M}$:

$K_{sp} = 6912 \left( \dfrac{s}{M} \right)^7$

Answer: $6912(\mathrm{~s} / \mathrm{M})^7$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An inorganic salt comprises of atoms of elements $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$. If the oxidation numbers of A, B and $\mathrm{C}$ are $+3,+6$ and $-$2 respectively, what is the possible formula of the compound?
questions.solution:
Let the formula of the compound be $\mathrm{A}_x(\mathrm{B}_y\mathrm{C}_z)_w$. The sum of oxidation states in a neutral compound must be zero.

Given oxidation numbers: $\mathrm{A} = +3$, $\mathrm{B} = +6$, $\mathrm{C} = -2$.

Consider the option $\mathrm{A}_2(\mathrm{BC}_4)_3$.

The total charge is calculated as: $2 \times (+3) + 3 \times [1 \times (+6) + 4 \times (-2)]$.

$= 6 + 3 \times [6 - 8] = 6 + 3 \times (-2) = 6 - 6 = 0$.

Since the sum of oxidation states is zero, the formula $\mathrm{A}_2(\mathrm{BC}_4)_3$ is electrically neutral and represents a possible inorganic salt.

Answer: $\mathrm{A}_2\left(\mathrm{BC}_4\right)_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the group of ions / molecules in which none of the species undergo Disproportionation reaction.
questions.solution:
A disproportionation reaction occurs when an element in a specific oxidation state is simultaneously oxidized and reduced. This requires the element to be in an intermediate oxidation state, meaning it must be capable of both increasing and decreasing its oxidation state.

Analyzing the species in option (r4BrP):
1. $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}$: The oxidation state of Cr is $+6$, which is the maximum possible oxidation state for Chromium. It cannot be further oxidized, so it cannot undergo disproportionation.
2. $\mathrm{F}_2$: Fluorine is the most electronegative element and is in its zero oxidation state. It can only be reduced to $-1$ (e.g., in $\mathrm{F}^{-}$). It cannot be oxidized, so it cannot undergo disproportionation.
3. $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}$: The oxidation state of Mn is $+7$, which is the maximum possible oxidation state for Manganese. It cannot be further oxidized, so it cannot undergo disproportionation.
4. $\mathrm{ClO}_4^{-}$: The oxidation state of Cl is $+7$, which is the maximum possible oxidation state for Chlorine. It cannot be further oxidized, so it cannot undergo disproportionation.

Since none of the species in $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}, \mathrm{F}_2, \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}, \mathrm{ClO}_4^{-}$ can undergo disproportionation, this is the correct group.

Answer: $\mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}, \mathrm{F}_2, \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}, \mathrm{ClO}_4{ }^{-}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The boiling point of a $4 \%$ aqueous solution of a non-volatile solute $\mathrm{P}$ is equal to the boiling point of $\mathrm{X} \%$ solution of another non-volatile solute $\mathrm{Q}$.
The relation between their Molar masses is $\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{Q}}=4 \mathrm{~Mp}$. What is $\mathrm{X}$ ?
questions.solution:
The elevation in boiling point is given by $\Delta T_b = K_b \times m$, where $m$ is the molality of the solution. Since the boiling points of the two solutions are equal, their elevations in boiling point are equal, which implies their molalities must be equal, assuming the solvent is the same and the solutes are non-volatile and non-electrolytic.

Let $w_P$ and $w_Q$ be the masses of solutes P and Q in $100 \text{ g}$ of solution. For a $4 \%$ solution of P, $w_P = 4 \text{ g}$ and the mass of solvent is $100 - 4 = 96 \text{ g}$. The molality $m_P$ is given by $m_P = \dfrac{w_P / M_P}{W_{solvent, P} / 1000} = \dfrac{4 / M_P}{96 / 1000} = \dfrac{4000}{96 M_P} = \dfrac{125}{3 M_P}$.

For an $X \%$ solution of Q, $w_Q = X \text{ g}$ and the mass of solvent is $100 - X \text{ g}$. The molality $m_Q$ is given by $m_Q = \dfrac{X / M_Q}{(100 - X) / 1000} = \dfrac{1000 X}{(100 - X) M_Q}$.

Equating $m_P$ and $m_Q$: $\dfrac{125}{3 M_P} = \dfrac{1000 X}{(100 - X) M_Q}$.

Given $M_Q = 4 M_P$, substitute this into the equation: $\dfrac{125}{3 M_P} = \dfrac{1000 X}{(100 - X) (4 M_P)}$.

Simplifying: $\dfrac{125}{3} = \dfrac{250 X}{100 - X} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2 X}{100 - X} \Rightarrow 100 - X = 6 X \Rightarrow 7 X = 100 \Rightarrow X = \dfrac{100}{7} \approx 14.2857$.

Rounding to two decimal places, $X = 14.29$.

Answer: 14.29

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the amount of ice that separates out on cooling a solution containing $60 \mathrm{~g}$ of Ethylene glycol in $250 \mathrm{~g}$ of water to $-9.3^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ ? $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}$ of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}=1.86 \mathrm{~K} / \mathrm{m} ;$ MM of ethylene glycol= $62 \mathrm{~amu}$
questions.solution:
The molar mass of ethylene glycol is $62 \text{ g/mol}$. The number of moles of ethylene glycol is $n = \dfrac{60}{62} \approx 0.9677 \text{ mol}$.

The freezing point depression formula is $\Delta T_f = K_f \times m$, where $m$ is the molality of the solution. Given $\Delta T_f = 0 - (-9.3) = 9.3 \text{ K}$ and $K_f = 1.86 \text{ K kg/mol}$, we have $9.3 = 1.86 \times m$.

Solving for molality $m$, we get $m = \dfrac{9.3}{1.86} = 5 \text{ mol/kg}$.

Molality is defined as $m = \dfrac{n}{W_{\text{solvent}} \text{ in kg}}$. Thus, $5 = \dfrac{0.9677}{W_{\text{solvent}}}$.

The mass of the remaining liquid water is $W_{\text{solvent}} = \dfrac{0.9677}{5} = 0.19354 \text{ kg} = 193.54 \text{ g}$.

The amount of ice that separates out is the initial mass of water minus the mass of water remaining in the solution: $250 \text{ g} - 193.54 \text{ g} = 56.46 \text{ g}$.

Answer: 56.46 g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\text { If a compound } \mathrm{X}_3 \mathrm{Y} \text { is } 60 \% \text { ionised in aqueous medium, what is its van't Hoff factor value? }$
questions.solution:
The compound $X_3Y$ dissociates in aqueous medium as follows:

$X_3Y \rightarrow 3X^{+} + Y^{3-}$

The number of ions produced per formula unit is $n = 3 + 1 = 4$.

The degree of dissociation is given as $\alpha = 60\% = 0.6$.

The van't Hoff factor $i$ is calculated using the formula $i = 1 + \alpha(n - 1)$.

Substituting the values $n = 4$ and $\alpha = 0.6$ into the formula:

$i = 1 + 0.6(4 - 1)$

$i = 1 + 0.6(3)$

$i = 1 + 1.8$

$i = 2.8$

Answer: 2.8

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}}$ for $\mathrm{O}_2$ at $293 \mathrm{~K}$ is $34.86 \mathrm{~kbar}$. What should be the partial pressure of $\mathrm{O}_2$ gas so that it has a solubility of $0.08 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{L}$ in water at $293 \mathrm{~K}$ ? (Density of solution $=1 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{ml}$)
questions.solution:
Henry's Law states that $P = K_{H} \times x$, where $P$ is the partial pressure of the gas, $K_{H}$ is Henry's constant, and $x$ is the mole fraction of the gas in the solution.

Given solubility of $O_{2} = 0.08 \text{ g/L}$. The molar mass of $O_{2}$ is $32 \text{ g/mol}$.

Number of moles of $O_{2}$ in $1 \text{ L}$ of solution = $\dfrac{0.08 \text{ g}}{32 \text{ g/mol}} = 0.0025 \text{ mol}$.

Density of solution = $1 \text{ g/mL} = 1000 \text{ g/L}$. Mass of $1 \text{ L}$ of solution = $1000 \text{ g}$.

Assuming the solution is dilute, the mass of water in $1 \text{ L}$ is approximately $1000 \text{ g}$.

Number of moles of water = $\dfrac{1000 \text{ g}}{18 \text{ g/mol}} \approx 55.55 \text{ mol}$.

Mole fraction of $O_{2}$ ($x$) = $\dfrac{n_{O_2}}{n_{O_2} + n_{H_2O}} \approx \dfrac{0.0025}{55.55} \approx 4.5 \times 10^{-5}$.

Given $K_{H} = 34.86 \text{ kbar} = 34860 \text{ bar}$.

Partial pressure $P = 34860 \text{ bar} \times 4.5 \times 10^{-5} \approx 1.5687 \text{ bar}$.

Rounding to the nearest value, $P \approx 1.569 \text{ bar}$.

Answer: 1.569 bar

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Above figure represents Vapour pressure versus Temperature graphs of 2 pure volatile liquids and a solution formed by the 2 liquids. (i) Which curve represents the solution? (ii) Which curve represents the liquid with the strongest intermolecular forces of attraction?
questions.solution:
The vapour pressure of a solution containing two volatile liquids is always intermediate between the vapour pressures of the two pure components at a given temperature. In the graph, curve A represents the liquid with the highest vapour pressure (weakest intermolecular forces), curve C represents the liquid with the lowest vapour pressure (strongest intermolecular forces), and curve B represents the solution formed by these two liquids.

Therefore, (i) curve B represents the solution, and (ii) curve C represents the liquid with the strongest intermolecular forces of attraction.

Answer: (i) B (ii) C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A given mass of a hydrocarbon on complete combustion produced $176 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and $90 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$. What is the Molecular formula of the compound?
questions.solution:
The combustion reaction of a hydrocarbon $C_xH_y$ is given by: $C_xH_y + (x + \dfrac{y}{4})O_2 \rightarrow xCO_2 + \dfrac{y}{2}H_2O$.

Calculate the moles of $CO_2$ produced: $n_{CO_2} = \dfrac{176 \text{ g}}{44 \text{ g/mol}} = 4 \text{ mol}$.

Calculate the moles of $H_2O$ produced: $n_{H_2O} = \dfrac{90 \text{ g}}{18 \text{ g/mol}} = 5 \text{ mol}$.

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, the moles of carbon atoms in the hydrocarbon equals the moles of $CO_2$, so $x = 4$.

The moles of hydrogen atoms in the hydrocarbon equals twice the moles of $H_2O$, so $y = 2 \times 5 = 10$.

The molecular formula of the hydrocarbon is $C_4H_{10}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{10}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below are 4 subatomic particles travelling with the same velocity "v". Which of them will have the shortest wavelength?
$[A]=\text { Proton }[B]=\text { Neutron. }[C]=\text { Alpha particle. }[D]=\text { Electron. }$
questions.solution:
According to the de Broglie hypothesis, the wavelength $\lambda$ of a particle moving with velocity $v$ is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{mv}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant and $m$ is the mass of the particle.

Since $h$ and $v$ are constant for all particles, the wavelength $\lambda$ is inversely proportional to the mass $m$ of the particle, i.e., $\lambda \propto \dfrac{1}{m}$.

To find the shortest wavelength, we must identify the particle with the largest mass among the given options:
Mass of electron ($m_e$) $\approx 9.1 \times 10^{-31}$ kg.
Mass of proton ($m_p$) $\approx 1.67 \times 10^{-27}$ kg.
Mass of neutron ($m_n$) $\approx 1.675 \times 10^{-27}$ kg.
Mass of alpha particle ($m_{\alpha}$) $\approx 4 \times m_p \approx 6.68 \times 10^{-27}$ kg.

Comparing the masses, the alpha particle has the largest mass among the given particles. Therefore, the alpha particle will have the shortest de Broglie wavelength.

Answer: [C]

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A statement of Assertion followed by a statement of Reason is given.
Choose the correct answer out of the following options.
Assertion : Energy of $2 \mathrm{~s}$ orbital of Hydrogen is less than the energy of the $2 \mathrm{~s}$ orbital of Lithium.
Reason : Energies of orbitals in the same subshell decrease with increase in atomic number.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are incorrect statements.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect statement.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct statement.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
questions.solution:
For a hydrogen-like atom or ion, the energy of an orbital with principal quantum number $n$ is given by $E_n = -13.6 \times \dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$ eV, where $Z$ is the atomic number.

For the $2s$ orbital of Hydrogen ($Z=1$), $E_{H, 2s} = -13.6 \times \dfrac{1^2}{2^2} = -3.4$ eV.

For the $2s$ orbital of Lithium ($Z=3$), $E_{Li, 2s} = -13.6 \times \dfrac{3^2}{2^2} = -13.6 \times 2.25 = -30.6$ eV.

Comparing the values, $-30.6$ eV is less than $-3.4$ eV, meaning the energy of the $2s$ orbital of Lithium is lower than that of Hydrogen. Thus, the Assertion is incorrect.

The Reason states that energies of orbitals in the same subshell decrease with an increase in atomic number. As shown by the formula $E_n \propto -Z^2$, as $Z$ increases, $Z^2$ increases, making the energy value more negative (i.e., lower). Therefore, the Reason is a correct statement.

Answer: Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct statement.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The mass number of an element $\mathrm{X}$ is 175 with 104 neutrons in its nucleus. Into which one of the following orbitals will the last electron enter?
questions.solution:
$Z = A - n = 175 - 104 = 71$

Element with $Z = 71$ is Lutetium (Lu). After Xe ($Z = 54$), 17 electrons are to be filled in order: $6s \rightarrow 4f \rightarrow 5d$

$6s$ gets 2, $4f$ gets 14, remaining 1 goes to $5d$.

Configuration: $[Xe]\ 6s^2\ 4f^{14}\ 5d^1$

The last electron enters the $5d$ orbital.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The standard enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{CH}_4$, the standard enthalpy of sublimation of Carbon and the bond dissociation enthalpy of Hydrogen gas are $-74.8,+719.6$ and $436 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$ respectively. What is the bond enthalpy of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ bond in Methane?
questions.solution:
The formation reaction of methane is given by: $\text{C(s)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_4\text{(g)}$. The enthalpy of this reaction is $\Delta_f H^{\circ} = -74.8 \text{ kJ/mol}$.

The atomization process involves the sublimation of carbon and the dissociation of hydrogen molecules:
1. $\text{C(s)} \rightarrow \text{C(g)}$, $\Delta H_1 = 719.6 \text{ kJ/mol}$
2. $2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 4\text{H(g)}$, $\Delta H_2 = 2 \times 436 = 872 \text{ kJ/mol}$

The total energy required to break all bonds in $\text{CH}_4$ to form gaseous atoms is the enthalpy of atomization of methane, $\Delta_{at} H^{\circ}$:
$\Delta_{at} H^{\circ} = \Delta H_1 + \Delta H_2 - \Delta_f H^{\circ}$
$\Delta_{at} H^{\circ} = 719.6 + 872 - (-74.8) = 719.6 + 872 + 74.8 = 1666.4 \text{ kJ/mol}$.

Since methane ($\text{CH}_4$) contains four $\text{C-H}$ bonds, the bond enthalpy of a single $\text{C-H}$ bond is:
$\text{Bond Enthalpy} = \dfrac{1666.4}{4} = 416.6 \text{ kJ/mol}$.

Answer: 416.6 kJ

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given: $\Delta \mathrm{G}^0{ }_{\mathrm{f}}$ of $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_2$ is $2.09 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol}$ and $\Delta \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{f}}^0$ of $\mathrm{C}_6 \mathrm{H}_6$ is $1.24 \times 10^5 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol}$.
Calculate the equilibrium constant for the cyclic polymerisation of Ethyne to Benzene at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. $(\mathrm{R}=8.314 \mathrm{JK}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1})$
questions.solution:
The reaction for the cyclic polymerization of ethyne to benzene is given by: $3C_{2}H_{2}(g) \rightarrow C_{6}H_{6}(l)$.

The standard Gibbs free energy change for the reaction, $\Delta G^{0}_{rxn}$, is calculated as:
$\Delta G^{0}_{rxn} = \sum \Delta G^{0}_{f}(products) - \sum \Delta G^{0}_{f}(reactants)$
$\Delta G^{0}_{rxn} = \Delta G^{0}_{f}(C_{6}H_{6}) - 3 \times \Delta G^{0}_{f}(C_{2}H_{2})$
$\Delta G^{0}_{rxn} = 1.24 \times 10^{5} - 3 \times (2.09 \times 10^{5})$
$\Delta G^{0}_{rxn} = 1.24 \times 10^{5} - 6.27 \times 10^{5} = -5.03 \times 10^{5} \text{ J/mol}$.

The relationship between $\Delta G^{0}$ and the equilibrium constant $K$ is given by $\Delta G^{0} = -RT \ln K$.
Given $T = 27^{\circ}C = 300 \text{ K}$ and $R = 8.314 \text{ J K}^{-1} \text{ mol}^{-1}$.
$-5.03 \times 10^{5} = -8.314 \times 300 \times \ln K$
$\ln K = \dfrac{5.03 \times 10^{5}}{8.314 \times 300}$
$\ln K = \dfrac{503000}{2494.2} \approx 201.667$.

$K = e^{201.667} \approx 1.429 \times 10^{87} \approx 1.429 \times 10^{88}$.

Answer: $1.429\times10^{88}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If the enthalpy of formation of a diatomic molecule $\mathrm{AB}$ is $-400 \mathrm{~kJ} / \mathrm{mol}$ and the bond dissociation energies of $\mathrm{A}_2$ and $\mathrm{B}_2$ and $\mathrm{AB}$ are in the ratio $2: 1: 2$, what is the bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{B}_2$ ?
questions.solution:
The formation reaction for the diatomic molecule $\mathrm{AB}$ is given by: $\dfrac{1}{2} \mathrm{A}_2(g) + \dfrac{1}{2} \mathrm{B}_2(g) \rightarrow \mathrm{AB}(g)$.

The enthalpy of formation $\Delta H_f^{\circ}$ is related to the bond dissociation energies (BDE) by the equation: $\Delta H_f^{\circ} = \sum \text{BDE}(\text{reactants}) - \sum \text{BDE}(\text{products})$.

Let the bond dissociation energies of $\mathrm{A}_2$, $\mathrm{B}_2$, and $\mathrm{AB}$ be $2x$, $x$, and $2x$ respectively, based on the given ratio $2:1:2$.

Substituting these into the enthalpy equation: $-400 = \left( \dfrac{1}{2}(2x) + \dfrac{1}{2}(x) \right) - (2x)$.

Simplifying the expression: $-400 = x + 0.5x - 2x$.

$-400 = -0.5x$.

Solving for $x$: $x = \dfrac{400}{0.5} = 800 \text{ kJ/mol}$.

Since the bond dissociation energy of $\mathrm{B}_2$ is $x$, the value is $800 \text{ kJ/mol}$.

Answer: 800 kJ/mol

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x)=2 x^3+9 x^2+\lambda x+20$ is a decreasing function of $x$ in the largest possible interval $(-2,-1)$, then $\lambda$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = 2x^3 + 9x^2 + \lambda x + 20$.

The derivative is $f'(x) = 6x^2 + 18x + \lambda$.

For $f(x)$ to be a decreasing function, $f'(x) \le 0$ for all $x$ in the interval $(-2, -1)$.

The quadratic $f'(x) = 6x^2 + 18x + \lambda$ represents a parabola opening upwards. For it to be non-positive in the interval $(-2, -1)$, the roots of $f'(x) = 0$ must be $-2$ and $-1$.

If the roots are $-2$ and $-1$, then $f'(x) = 6(x + 2)(x + 1) = 6(x^2 + 3x + 2) = 6x^2 + 18x + 12$.

Comparing $6x^2 + 18x + 12$ with $6x^2 + 18x + \lambda$, we get $\lambda = 12$.

Checking the condition, $f'(x) = 6(x+2)(x+1) \le 0$ for $x \in [-2, -1]$, which satisfies the requirement.

Answer: $12$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The most economical proportion of the height of a covered box of fixed volume whose base is a rectangle with one side three times as long as the other, is
options: Equal to shorter side of base
questions.solution:
Let the sides of the rectangular base be $x$ and $3x$. Let the height of the box be $h$.

The volume $V$ of the box is given by $V = (x)(3x)(h) = 3x^2 h$. Since $V$ is fixed, $h = \dfrac{V}{3x^2}$.

The surface area $S$ of the covered box is $S = 2(length \times width + width \times height + height \times length) = 2(3x^2 + 3xh + xh) = 2(3x^2 + 4xh)$.

Substituting $h = \dfrac{V}{3x^2}$ into the surface area equation:

$S = 6x^2 + 8x \left( \dfrac{V}{3x^2} \right) = 6x^2 + \dfrac{8V}{3x}$.

To minimize $S$, differentiate with respect to $x$ and set to zero:

$\dfrac{dS}{dx} = 12x - \dfrac{8V}{3x^2} = 0$.

$12x = \dfrac{8V}{3x^2} \Rightarrow 36x^3 = 8V \Rightarrow V = \dfrac{36x^3}{8} = \dfrac{9x^3}{2}$.

Substitute $V$ back into the expression for $h$:

$h = \dfrac{9x^3 / 2}{3x^2} = \dfrac{3x}{2}$.

The height $h$ is $\dfrac{3}{2}$ times the shorter side of the base $x$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2} \times$ shorter side of base

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The side of an equilateral triangle expands at the rate of $\sqrt{3} \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{sec}$. When the side is $12 \mathrm{~cm}$, the rate of increase of its area is
questions.solution:
$A = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot a \cdot \dfrac{da}{dt}$

Substituting $a = 12$ cm and $\dfrac{da}{dt} = \sqrt{3}$ cm/sec:

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 12 \times \sqrt{3} = \dfrac{\sqrt{3} \times 12 \times \sqrt{3}}{2} = \dfrac{36}{2} = 18$ cm$^2$/sec
